$comment: CANONICAL runner-failure signal table — the single source of truth for every surface.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. Yaver classifies runner failures on web (TypeScript), the Go
agent, mobile/RN, tvOS (Swift), watchOS (Swift), Wear OS (Kotlin) and visionOS
(Swift). Native surfaces cannot import web/lib, so every one of them is an
INDEPENDENT copy — and this repo has already paid for that twice: three relay-auth
matchers drifted apart with none a superset of the others, and on 2026-08-02 every
single matcher was missing Anthropic's actual OAuth-expiry wording, so the commonest
runner failure there is produced no route on any surface.
So the strings live HERE, once. Each surface embeds them; web/lib/failureSignalParity.test.ts
reads every surface's source and fails when one cannot name a cause another can.
Adding a signal means adding it here AND to each surface in the same change — the
parity test is what makes that non-optional.
THE LAW THIS TABLE ENCODES: a failure that is not about the credential must never
route the user into a sign-in flow. Billing, throttling, model entitlement and a
missing provider key are all valid credentials failing for other reasons; sending
someone through OAuth for any of them is a dead end that also destroys a working
session in the rate-limit case.

auth.meaning: The runner's own OAuth grant is no longer accepted.
auth.action: Sign the runner in again on that machine (Remote OAuth, or over SSH).

auth-revoked.meaning: The grant was revoked server-side. A refresh cannot recover it.
auth-revoked.action: Sign in again to issue a brand-new credential.
signals: oauth access token has been revoked

billing.meaning: The credential is valid; the account cannot pay for the call.
billing.action: Top up or upgrade that provider account. Signing in again will not help.

rate-limit.meaning: Throttled. The credential and the model are both fine.
rate-limit.action: Wait for the limit to reset and retry. Do NOT sign in again — a fresh token does not reset a quota, and re-auth throws away a working session.

model-not-supported.meaning: The signed-in plan does not include the selected model.
model-not-supported.action: Pick a different model for this machine. Signing in again cannot move a model onto a plan.
signals: does not have access to model

model-not-found.meaning: The runner could not resolve the model id at all.
model-not-found.action: Pick a model this runner lists on this machine. OpenCode ids must be written <providerId>/<modelId>.

provider-key.meaning: The PROVIDER's API key is missing or rejected. Unrelated to Yaver sign-in and to the runner's OAuth.
provider-key.action: Set that provider's API key on the machine (env var, opencode.json options.apiKey, or /connect).

$comment: How a runner proves itself decides which failures it can even have.
An API-key runner has no OAuth grant, so token_expired / revoked / refresh_token_reused
are impossible for it — during an OAuth outage it is structurally immune, not merely
an alternative. Measured on the owner's fleet: opencode on magara reports
authSource 'GLM API key' and kept working while codex had no credentials at all.
An unrecognised label stays 'unknown' and is NEVER guessed into a bucket: recommending
a mislabelled OAuth runner is worst exactly when OAuth is what broke.
